context: Starting at [0, 0] in a grid of nonnegative numbers, a path may move only right or down. Both its start and end count toward the sum. The entry dp[i, j] is the minimum path sum to row i, column j, with both indices ranging from 0 to 3. Two 4×4 symbolic dp tables illustrate “Boundary conditions: initialize the first row and column” on the left and “State transition order: traverse the matrix in forward order” on the right. The grid's numeric values are omitted.
description: The left table marks the upper-left starting cell in green, the rest of the first row in blue, and the rest of the first column in purple. Arrows point right along the first row and down the first column. Arrows in the right table show that an interior cell depends on the already computed states above it and to its left. Both tables use only symbolic entries such as dp[0,0] through dp[3,3].

Initialize the start, then accumulate values along the only route to each cell in the first row and first column. Fill the nine interior cells with row index i = 1, 2, 3 in the outer loop and column index j = 1, 2, 3 in the inner loop. When computing dp[i,j], the entry above it, dp[i-1,j], is ready from the previous row, and the entry to its left, dp[i,j-1], is ready from the current row. The formulas in the table follow from the boundaries and predecessors shown. The original figure does not spell them out individually.

frames.explanation: After the start, each first-row or first-column cell has only one predecessor. Only interior cells need to take the minimum of the predecessors above and to the left.
frames.title: Initialize the first row and column, then fill the table in forward row-major order

summary: Set the starting value, then initialize the boundaries by accumulating values to the right along the first row and downward along the first column. Fill the interior from top to bottom, moving left to right within each row.
